certainty_reasoning: Queensberry's plea contains a Schwabe clause (22 November 1892, Paris) which, as printed by Hyde, avers solicitation and incitement only, with no 'did commit' clause.
summary: Maurice Salis Schwabe, nephew by marriage of Solicitor-General Sir Frank Lockwood, was the connective figure of the circle: he introduced Wilde to Taylor, gave the Kettner's dinner at which Mavor met Wilde, and was named at the libel trial only on paper passed to counsel. Atkins testified to finding the twenty-two-year-old Schwabe in bed with Wilde at 29 Boulevard des Capucines in November 1892 — testimony from a witness whose credibility was destroyed at the same trial. The plea's Schwabe clause alleges solicitation only, and Schwabe, abroad, was never called.

disputed.claim: that Schwabe shared Wilde's bed in Paris (November 1892) and that Wilde solicited him to commit sodomy
disputed.asserted_by: Fred Atkins's sworn testimony, Regina v. Wilde and Taylor, 26 April 1895 (Hyde p. 207); Queensberry's plea of justification, 22 November 1892 clause (solicit/incite only as printed)
disputed.disputed_by: the collapse of Atkins's credibility (perjury exposed, ordered from the box, Hyde pp. 217-218; jury not guilty on the Atkins counts); Wilde's general denials; no charge ever laid concerning Schwabe and no testimony from Schwabe himself
disputed.grounds: sole eyewitness discredited; the plea clause as printed lacks the 'did … commit' averment made against the other named men

sources.supports: The sole eyewitness claim of Schwabe in Wilde's bed, Paris, November 1892 — from a witness later discredited for perjury; the class-deciding quote
sources.speaker: Frederick Atkins, examination-in-chief

sources.quote: And that the said Oscar Fingal O'Flahertie Wills Wilde on the twenty-second day of November in the year of our Lord One thousand eight hundred and ninety-two at the said house in Paris did solicit and incite one Maurice Salis Schwabe to commit sodomy and other acts of gross indecency and immorality with the said Maurice Salis Schwabe.
sources.context: Queensberry's plea of justification, filed 30 March 1895; Hyde's Appendix A from the Central Criminal Court records. Note: unlike the Atkins, Wood, Parker, Scarfe, Grainger and Conway clauses, no 'did then and there commit' averment follows
sources.supports: The formal allegation — solicitation/incitement only as printed
sources.speaker: The Marquess of Queensberry, plea of justification (filed 30 March 1895)
